messages:
maria (infra): seeing recurrent latency spikes from dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-west-2 this morning, looks like cross-tenant egress flapping around 10:02 UTC. top of stack shows sustained packet drops on eth1, flows tied to a handful of tenants.
raj (network): do you have a pcap or tc qdisc dump? could be NIC interrupt storm or a shared vSwitch oversubscribe.
maria (infra): attaching quick capture excerpt below (trimmed):
```
10:02:13.123 IP tenant-A -> internet 1450 bytes seq 1..1450
10:02:13.124 IP tenant-B -> internet 1450 bytes seq 1..1450
10:02:13.125 IP tenant-A -> internet 1450 bytes seq 1451..2900
... many retransmits, burst every ~200ms
```
anton (scheduling): tenants A/B are on the same slice (slice-17) because of packing, we recently reduced slices to save capacity. might be a noisy neighbor.
kim (prod-eng): hmm we moved some high-throughput inference jobs to slice-17 last night (batching tests). could be saturating egress at the bridge.
nina (oncall): alert pipeline flagged p50 token latency +120ms over baseline for queries routed through eu-west-proxy-03. correlating with NIC error counters now.
sre-bot: [alert] egress.packet_loss > 5% on pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-west-2 for last 6m
raj (network): thinking VLAN-level shielding might help — isolate tenant slices into separate VLANs on the leaf switch so they don't compete on L2 broadcast domains and avoid mac learning storms. also can apply per-VLAN policing.
maria (infra): VLAN shielding sounds good but we need minimal blast radius and no reboots. can we do per-slice macvlan/tagging in OVS and program tc policing in-kernel?
raj (network): yes, we can use macvlan on top of the existing bond, then create per-tenant veth namespaces + tc tbf egress limits. example snippet to test on a single node:
```
# create macvlan for slice-17
ip link add link bond0 name mv-slice17 type macvlan mode bridge
ip link set mv-slice17 up
# attach namespace and shape
ip netns add ns-test
ip link set mv-slice17 netns ns-test
ip netns exec ns-test tc qdisc add dev mv-slice17 root tbf rate 500mbit burst 32k latency 50ms
```
anton (scheduling): can we do this non-destructively at scale? we have ~120 nodes in eu-west pool.
raj (network): start with a canary on 3 nodes. if stable, roll agent to convert slice assignment to tag traffic and update the node NIC config via cloud-init or daemonset.
kim (prod-eng): alternative: per-slice proxy fallback — if slice egress is saturated, transparently route that tenant's outbound via an internal NAT proxy on a different AZ with more headroom. flips are cheaper than rebuilding NIC configs.
maria (infra): proxy fallback seems lower-risk for short-term mitigation. but cost + latency tradeoff? we measured an extra 20-40ms cross-AZ earlier. some customers' SLOs won't accept that.
anton (scheduling): proposal: two-step — (1) quick mitigation: enable proxy-fallback for non-latency-sensitive jobs (batching experiments) and set threshold triggers; (2) long-term: VLAN/macvlan shielding + tc shaping for strict isolation.
nina (oncall): +1. can we get runbook changes? also want a dashboard widget showing per-slice egress drops and which proxies are being used.
raj (network): i'll own canary VLAN config and tc script. maria, can you do the proxy-fallback patch (routing policy + feature flag)? kim/anton, please produce list of tenants to exclude from fallback (low-latency customers).
maria (infra): will open a PR for routing policy flags and a short feature-flag rollout plan. drafting runbook here:
- detect: egress.packet_loss > 3% OR egress.qdisc_drop > 1000/min for any slice
- action-1 (auto): enable proxy-fallback for slice (if slice.label != low-latency)
- action-2 (manual): start VLAN shielding canary on N=3 nodes, monitor 15m
- rollback: revert proxy-fallback and drain canary nodes if errors increase
kim (prod-eng): please tag the canary with 'no-evict' so scheduling doesn't move critical workloads into canary during test.
anton (scheduling): will add policy. also suggest a brief audit to see which slices have high egress variance over last 7d, to prioritize permanent isolation.
raj (network): timeline: canary config today late-afternoon, proxy-fallback PR for review in 1h, rollout to auto-flag in staging in 2h.
nina (oncall): i'm coordinating alerts and will be on-call during rollout window. please ping #oncall when you start.
sre-bot: [action] created incident ticket INF-2024-358 with runbook link: https://redwood.internal/infra/incidents/INF-2024-358
maria (infra): thanks all — will post PR link and canary node list shortly.
raj (network): quick note: if we do macvlan we must ensure MTU preserved and avoid promiscuous issues on cloud provider bridges. watch for PMTU/icmp fragmentation errors.
kim (prod-eng): acknowledged. also capture perf baseline before canary: p50/p95 tokens, egress throughput, and kernel drop counters.
maria (infra): baseline captured, starting proxy-fallback PR now. will update thread with timestamps.
anton (scheduling): logging: add a tag in allocation metadata when a tenant hits proxy-fallback so we can trace request paths end-to-end.
kim (prod-eng): and please surface cost delta per-tenant when proxy used (egress proxy bandwidth + cross-AZ egress). finance wants quick estimate.
nina (oncall): prepping post-mortem template in case canary triggers degraded service.
maria (infra): ok launching canary checklist in 30m. I'll ping here at start. :white_check_mark:
